abstract: Maintains onboard trauma care facility certification and en-route stabilization performance records
system_message:
You are Emergency Medical Director (MEDDIR). As the Emergency Medical Director (MEDDIR), you maintain onboard trauma care facility certification and en-route stabilization performance records, overseeing designated evacuation cabin suite configurations, clinical simulation audits, and dedicated aeromedical gas storage inventories.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains onboard trauma care facility certification and en-route stabilization performance records（MEDCARE）
information_points.content:
MEDDIR-MEDCARE-IY1：For the Ekofisk Complex Sector Staged Transfer flight plan, the aeromedical cabin readiness register confirms that the designated evacuation cabin suite is configured for trauma life-support. According to clinical simulation audit records for simulated severe hypothermic polytrauma intake, the critical airway stabilization duration is 10 min.
MEDDIR-MEDCARE-FDP：For the Aberdeen Cross-Basin High-Speed Corridor flight plan, the aeromedical cabin readiness register verifies that the designated evacuation cabin suite is configured for trauma life-support. Clinical simulation audit records document a critical airway stabilization duration of 10 min under simulated severe hypothermic polytrauma intake conditions.
MEDDIR-MEDCARE-E78：For the Stavanger Deepwater Direct Insertion flight plan, the designated evacuation cabin suite is confirmed to be configured for trauma life-support in the aeromedical cabin readiness register. Clinical simulation audit records indicate a critical airway stabilization duration of 22 min during simulated severe hypothermic polytrauma intake.

information_points.title: Medical oxygen inventory（OXYGEN）
information_points.content:
MEDDIR-OXYGEN-PGU：For the Ekofisk Complex Sector Staged Transfer flight plan, the biomedical gas audit confirms a pressurized medical oxygen reserve volume of 3000 L across certified dedicated aeromedical oxygen storage cylinders.
MEDDIR-OXYGEN-Y55：For the Stavanger Deepwater Direct Insertion flight plan, the biomedical gas audit records a pressurized medical oxygen reserve volume of 4500 L across dedicated aeromedical oxygen storage cylinders.
MEDDIR-OXYGEN-725：For the Aberdeen Cross-Basin High-Speed Corridor flight plan, certified dedicated aeromedical oxygen storage cylinders provide a pressurized medical oxygen reserve volume of 6000 L according to the biomedical gas audit.
